planning/plan.md:3:This plan maps all 114 [specification requirements](spec.md) to build steps and acceptance checks. The [implementation and acceptance record](#implementation-and-acceptance-record) gives the status of the build, Section 508 checks, and final submission.
planning/plan.md:88:12. **Verify Section 508 accessibility for the delivered CLI and documentation.** Spec lines R-106–R-114.
planning/plan.md:172:| TP-53 · Step 12 · software criteria · A-107 | Inventory each delivered interface, platform and multistep workflow. Reuse the TP-52 terminal and assistive-technology setup. | TP-52 replay for operator workflows. | Map the applicable WCAG 2.0 A and AA criteria and conformance requirements, Chapter 5 requirements and E204.1 Chapter 3 criteria to test results. Apply the E207.2 exceptions for criteria 2.4.1, 2.4.5, 3.2.3 and 3.2.4 and WCAG Conformance Requirement 3, then apply E207.2.1 terminology substitutions and evaluate all software steps under E207.3. Verify applicable interoperability and that the CLI does not disrupt platform accessibility settings. | `planning/spec.md` R-107 and its cited Revised 508 Standards provisions. | R-107 |
planning/plan.md:358:- **Step 12.** The CLI text mode and report structure changes shipped. The current suite passed all 115 tests, including TP-54’s automated regression. The documentation review also replayed interruption, recovery and export in both JSON and text with a two-second timeout and ordinary claim expiry in temporary workspaces. The [accessibility evidence](../deliverables/verification.md#section-508-accessibility) records keyboard operation, rendered document structure, and Orca navigation of the mixed-state queue. TP-55 and TP-57 are inapplicable to this CLI-only release without an application support service.
planning/plan.md:359:- **Open Section 508 acceptance checks.** Complete the screen-reader replay beyond queue navigation (TP-52 and TP-54), including help, progress, history, export and accuracy. Record the effects of supported platform accessibility settings and complete the criterion-level review (TP-53). Verify rendered-document navigation with assistive technology and follow the handover with it (TP-56). Close TP-58 when all applicable results and reasons for inapplicability are recorded. Section 508 conformance remains unverified.
deliverables/verification.md:68:## Section 508 accessibility
deliverables/verification.md:70:Step 12 covers the internal CLI, its operator-facing outputs, and the rendered README, accuracy report and verification report. Operators need to identify requests and their state without color or vision, operate without a mouse or timed input, keep their terminal preferences, and recover interrupted or failed work using the same information and permissions. The application ships a local CLI. There is no public workflow, application web UI, or application support service in this build. R-110 and R-113 are inapplicable for that reason. [Revised 508 Standards](https://www.access-board.gov/ict/) · [WCAG 2.0](https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG20/)
deliverables/verification.md:91:| R-109 | A-109 and `test_r109_contract`, CLI text | The regression verifies labels, reading order, state, owner, action and retry, progress, history and report output with no terminal escape or cursor-rewrite sequences. The Orca queue navigation check passed as recorded below. |
deliverables/verification.md:98:### Orca queue navigation
deliverables/verification.md:100:On November 19, 2026, a keyboard-only replay used Ubuntu 24.04, Xfce Terminal 1.1.3, Orca 46.1 and `less` 590 in a virtual desktop. Speech Dispatcher used eSpeak NG and a virtual PulseAudio sink. The replay captured Orca's spoken text from the Speech Dispatcher log and confirmed that the sink received audio.
deliverables/verification.md:109:Press `g` for the first request. For the later requests, press `g` and search with `/Document: IT-002` or `/Document: IT-010`. In Orca's desktop layout, use `Insert` + numpad `7` to read the first visible line and numpad `9` to read each next line. Use numpad minus to leave flat review before returning to pager navigation. The spoken lines followed this order within each request.
deliverables/verification.md:111:| Request | What Orca read during navigation |
deliverables/verification.md:115:| IT-010.json | Document identifier, work state Failed, owner IT Service Desk, status `error`, next action `retry-extraction`, the provider error, and the retry command. Orca read both terminal lines of the wrapped command in sequence. |
deliverables/verification.md:133:| WCAG 4.1.1–4.1.2, 502 | The platform presents the CLI through an ordinary terminal text control. The renderer provides native HTML headings, links and table headers. The application supplies no platform accessibility service or custom controls. AT-SPI and screen-reader observations assess interoperability and non-disruption separately from the structured text checks. |

pulse_modules=$(dirname "$(find "$root_trial/usr/lib" -name module-null-sink.so -print -quit)")

for i in {1..45}; do
    if pactl info >"$work/pulse-info.txt" 2>/dev/null; then break; fi
    sleep .1
done
pactl list short sinks || { cat "$work/pulse.log"; exit 1; }
parecord --device=intake_audit.monitor --file-format=wav "$work/speech.wav" >"$work/parecord.log" 2>&1 &
record_pid=$!

trap 'for pid in ${terminal_pid:-} ${orca_pid:-} ${speech_pid:-} ${wm_pid:-} ${registry_pid:-} ${bus_pid:-} ${worker_pid:-} "$x_pid" "$record_pid" "$pulse_pid"; do kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; done' EXIT
orca --debug --debug-file "$work/orca.log" --enable=speech >"$work/orca-stderr.log" 2>&1 &
orca_pid=$!
sleep 1
cd "$repo"
.venv/bin/python -m intake run --input "$work/input" --db "$work/intake.db" --provider mock \

worker_pid=$!
for i in {1..80}; do
    if test -e "$work/gates/entered" &&
        .venv/bin/python -m intake queue --db "$work/intake.db" --include-pending --format text >"$work/wait.txt" &&

    sleep .1
done

cat >"$work/bashrc" <<'RC'
PS1='queue-test$ '

show_queue() {
    "$repo/.venv/bin/python" -m intake queue --db "$work/intake.db" --include-pending --format text >"$work/queue.txt"
    LESS= less -j1 "$work/queue.txt"
}
RC
xfce4-terminal --disable-server --font='DejaVu Sans Mono 12' --geometry=126x42 --title='Orca Queue' \
    --command="/bin/bash --rcfile $work/bashrc -i" >"$work/terminal.log" 2>&1 &
terminal_pid=$!
window=$(timeout 10 xdotool search --sync --onlyvisible --name 'Orca Queue' | head -n 1)
test -n "$window"
timeout 8 xdotool windowactivate --sync "$window"
xdotool type --clearmodifiers --delay 25 show_queue
xdotool key Return
for i in {1..55}; do
    if test -s "$work/queue.txt"; then break; fi
    sleep .1
done
sleep 1
for document in IT-001 IT-002 IT-010; do
    xdotool key --clearmodifiers g

        xdotool type --clearmodifiers "Document: $document"
        xdotool key Return

    sleep 1
    wc -l < "$work/orca.log" > "$work/$document-nav-start.txt"
    xdotool key --clearmodifiers Insert+KP_Home
    sleep 1.5
    for i in {1..9}; do
        xdotool key --clearmodifiers KP_Prior
        sleep 1.2
    done
    xdotool key --clearmodifiers KP_Subtract
    sleep .5
    wc -l < "$work/orca.log" > "$work/$document-nav-end.txt"
done
xdotool key --clearmodifiers q
sleep 1
for document in IT-001 IT-002 IT-010; do

    sed -n "$((start+1)),${end}p" "$work/orca.log" | rg "SPEECH DISPATCHER: Speaking '[[:space:]]*(Document|Work state|Owner|Status|Next action|Error|Retry command)"
done

L0: # Information and Communication Technology

L2: ### Revised 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines
L3: ## About the ICT Accessibility 508 Standards and 255 Guidelines
L4: 
L5: These standards address access to information and communication technology (ICT) under Section 508 of the Rehabilitation Act and Section 255 of the Communications Act.
L6: Section 508 of the 【0†Rehabilitation Act】 charges the Access Board with developing and promulgating this rule.  The statute also charges the Access Board with providing Technical Assistance on Section 508, which is provided through 【1†webinars】, 【2†trainings】, and in close collaboration with GSA and materials available from 【3†Section508.gov†www.section508.gov】.
L7: Section 508 requires access to ICT developed, procured, maintained, or used by federal agencies.  Examples include computers, telecommunications equipment, multifunction office machines such as copiers that also operate as printers, software, websites, information kiosks and transaction machines, and electronic documents.  The Section 508 Standards, which are part of the Federal Acquisition Regulation, ensure access for people with physical, sensory, or cognitive disabilities.
L8: The Section 255 Guidelines cover telecommunications equipment and customer-premises equipment — such as telephones, cell phones, routers, set-top boxes, and computers with modems, interconnected Voice over Internet Protocol products, and software integral to the operation of telecommunications function of such equipment.
L9: ### Background
L10:   * January 22, 2018 – The Board issues 【4†correction to the final rule†federalregister.gov】 to restore provisions for TTY access.

citeturn2view3 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: today; Content type: text/html; Source: find({"ref_id":"https://www.access-board.gov/ict/","pattern":"503.2 User Preferences"}); Total lines: 2383
L195: #### E203.2 User Needs
L196: 
L197: When agencies procure, develop, maintain or use ICT they shall identify the needs of users with disabilities to determine:
L198: 
L199:   1. How users with disabilities will perform the functions supported by the ICT; and
L200:   2. How the ICT will be developed, installed, configured, and maintained to support users with disabilities.
L201: 
L202: ### E204 Functional Performance Criteria
L877: #### 502.4 Platform Accessibility Features
L878: 
L880:   1. Section 9.3.3 Enable sequential entry of multiple (chorded) keystrokes;
L881:   2. Section 9.3.4 Provide adjustment of delay before key acceptance;
L882:   3. Section 9.3.5 Provide adjustment of same-key double-strike acceptance;
L883:   4. Section 10.6.7 Allow users to choose visual alternative for audio output;
L884:   5. Section 10.6.8 Synchronize audio equivalents for visual events;
L885:   6. Section 10.6.9 Provide speech output services; and
L886:   7. Section 10.7.1 Display any captions provided.
L887: ### 503 Applications
L888: 
L889: #### 503.1 General
L890: 
L891: Applications shall conform to 503.
L892: 
L893: #### 503.2 User Preferences
L894: 
L895: Applications shall permit user preferences from platform settings for color, contrast, font type, font size, and focus cursor.
L896: EXCEPTION: Applications that are designed to be isolated from their underlying platform software, including Web applications, shall not be required to conform to 503.2.
L897: #### 503.3 Alternative User Interfaces
L898: 
L899: Where an application provides an alternative user interface that functions as assistive technology, the application shall use platform and other industry standard accessibility services.
L900: 
L901: #### 503.4 User Controls for Captions and Audio Description
L902: 
L903: Where ICT displays video with synchronized audio, ICT shall provide user controls for closed captions and audio descriptions conforming to 503.4.
L904: ##### 503.4.1 Caption Controls
L905: 
L906: Where user controls are provided for volume adjustment, ICT shall provide user controls for the selection of captions at the same menu level as the user controls for volume or program selection.
L907: 
L908: ##### 503.4.2 Audio Description Controls
L909: 
L910: Where user controls are provided for program selection, ICT shall provide user controls for the selection of audio descriptions at the same menu level as the user controls for volume or program selection.
L911: 
L912: ### 504 Authoring Tools
L913: #### 504.1 General
L914: 
L915: Where an application is an authoring tool, the application shall conform to 504 to the extent that information required for accessibility is supported by the destination format.
L916: #### 504.2 Content Creation or Editing
L917: Authoring tools shall provide a mode of operation to create or edit content that conforms to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1) for all supported features and, as applicable, to file formats supported by the authoring tool. Authoring tools shall permit authors the option of overriding information required for accessibility.
L1964: One ICT company recommended adding some additional requirements for assistive technology interoperability that parallel clauses 11.3.2.2 and 11.3.2.3 in EN 301 549. The Board declines to follow this recommendation as we have determined that 502.3 in the final rule already contains equivalent technical requirements for assistive technology interoperability, and is simpler and more practical to apply relative to the EN approach, without compromising accessibility.
L1965: ##### 503 Applications
L1966: The proposed rule included a general requirement that applications must permit users to set their preferences from platform settings for color, contrast, font type, and focus cursor (proposed 503.2). For example, a user with low vision might want the default windowing scheme to use yellow on black text with an 18 point sans-serif font.
L1967: An exception to this provision exempts applications that are designed to be isolated from their underlying platform software (such as Web applications) from this requirement. We received several comments (from individuals, a disability advocacy organization, and an accessibility ICT services provider) concerning the scope of the exception.
L1968: These commenters acknowledged that certain technologies (such as Adobe® Flash®) were properly exempted, but thought that the exception was otherwise overbroad by sweeping in other types of Web applications (which were unspecified). More generally, some of these commenters also suggested that the Board broaden 503.2 so that the requirement for pass-through of user preferences apply to Web content, as well as applications.
L1969: With respect to commenters' suggestion of overbreadth, the Board declines to revise the exception to apply only to certain types of Web applications. We are aware of no discernible basis for differentiating between Web applications that do and do not warrant the exception, nor did commenters offer any such criteria.
L1970: It is not technically feasible to require Web applications to use platform preferences because generally the developer of a Web application has no way of knowing what font characteristics a reader will be using for text in windows of their operating system. Applications, including Web applications, which qualify for the exception to use platform settings are still subject to the other requirements of Chapter 5, including the requirements referenced by WCAG 2.0 Level AA.
L1971: Likewise, the Board finds commenters' suggestion that the scope of proposed 502.3 be broadened to include Web content to be misplaced. Section 502.3 in the final rule, as with all of Chapter 5, addresses technical requirements for accessibility of software, not Web content. In any event, requiring Web content to meet requirements for pass-through of user preferences would face the same technical challenges as Web applications.
L1972: ##### 504 Authoring Tools
L1973: This section contains additional requirements for software used to create and edit content and documents. The major substantive change from the proposed rule is the addition of a new requirement (final 504.2.2) that authoring tools capable of creating full-featured PDFs (that is, a PDF that conforms to PDF 1.7, also known as ISO 32000-1) must also support creating PDFs conforming to PDF/UA-1.
L1974: PDF/UA-1 is an extension to PDF 1.7, meaning that PDF/UA-1 is only applicable to PDFs that already conform to PDF 1.7.
L1975: Based on comments from a standards developing organization, an ICT trade association, and an ICT company, we have made some editorial changes to proposed sections 504.2, 504.3, and 504.4 for the final rule. For example, "all features and formats" in the proposed rule have been changed to "all supported features and, as applicable, to file formats" in the final rule, to clarify that the limitations of the file formats be taken into consideration.
L1976: A disability advocacy organization commented that the accessibility features should be turned on by default, but the Board has decided that would be overly prescriptive. In addition, such a requirement could interfere with automated testing of content for accessibility features. For example, it is significantly easier to identify missing alternative text (as an error) than it is to test for overuse of placeholder or default alternative text.

mapfile -t bus < <(dbus-daemon --fork --config-file="$trial/at-spi.conf" --print-address=1 --print-pid=1)
export AT_SPI_BUS_ADDRESS="\${bus[0]}"

"$root_trial/usr/libexec/at-spi2-registryd" >"$work/registry.log" 2>&1 &

"$trial/speech-dispatcher" -s -l 4 -L "$work/speech/log" -C "$work/speech" -m "$root_trial/usr/lib/speech-dispatcher-modules" -S "$work/run/speechd.sock" -P "$work/run/speechd.pid" >"$work/speechd.log" 2>&1 &
pids+=("$!")

pids+=("$!")

PS1='intake-test$ '
cd "$repo"
oper() { python -m intake "$@"; }
begin() {
    python -m intake run --input "$work/input" --db "$work/intake.db" --provider mock --responses tests/mock_responses --script "$work/initial.json" --mock-gates "$work/gates" --timeout 9 --format text >"$work/start.out" 2>&1 &

write_report() { oper accuracy --input materials/requests --synthetic tests/fixtures/IT-P01.json --expected tests/expected --provider mock --output "$work/accuracy.md" --format text >"$work/accuracy.out"; }
operator_help() { oper queue --help >"$work/help.out"; }
pager() { LESS= less -j1 "$work/$1.out"; }

REDACTED

xfce4-terminal --disable-server --geometry=120x34 --title='Northstar Orca' --command="/bin/bash --rcfile $work/bashrc -i" >"$work/terminal.log" 2>&1 &
pids+=("$!")

await_file() { for i in {1..70}; do if test -s "$1"; then return; fi; sleep .1; done; return 1; }

test -s "$work/export/queue.json"
read_page() {
    local name="$1" search="$2" lines="$3" start

gi.require_version('Atspi', '2.0')

image.savev(str(work / f'{sys.argv[1]}.png'), 'png', [], [])

L913: #### 504.1 General
L914: 
L915: Where an application is an authoring tool, the application shall conform to 504 to the extent that information required for accessibility is supported by the destination format.
L916: #### 504.2 Content Creation or Editing
L917: Authoring tools shall provide a mode of operation to create or edit content that conforms to Level A and Level AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements in WCAG 2.0 (incorporated by reference, see 702.10.1) for all supported features and, as applicable, to file formats supported by the authoring tool. Authoring tools shall permit authors the option of overriding information required for accessibility.
L918: EXCEPTION: Authoring tools shall not be required to conform to 504.2 when used to directly edit plain text source code.

L920: 
L921: Authoring tools shall, when converting content from one format to another or saving content in multiple formats, preserve the information required for accessibility to the extent that the information is supported by the destination format.
L922: ##### 504.2.2 PDF Export
L923: 
L924: Authoring tools capable of exporting PDF files that conform to ISO 32000-1:2008 (PDF 1.7) shall also be capable of exporting PDF files that conform to ANSI/AIIM/ISO 14289-1:2016 (PDF/UA-1) (incorporated by reference, see 702.3.1).
L925: #### 504.3 Prompts

L928: #### 504.4 Templates

L781: 
L782: Digital television tuners shall provide audio description processing that conforms to ATSC A/53 Digital Television Standard, Part 5 (2014) (incorporated by reference, see 702.2.1). L869: Applications shall expose information and mechanisms necessary to track focus, text insertion point, and selection attributes of user interface components.
L870: 
L871: ##### 502.3.13 Modification of Focus Cursor
L872: 
L873: Focus, text insertion point, and selection attributes that can be set by the user shall be capable of being set programmatically, including through the use of assistive technology.
L874: ##### 502.3.14 Event Notification
L875: 
L876: Notification of events relevant to user interactions, including but not limited to, changes in the component’s state(s), value, name, description, or boundary, shall be available to assistive technology.
L877: #### 502.4 Platform Accessibility Features
L878: 
L879: Platforms and platform software shall conform to the requirements in ANSI/HFES 200.2, Human Factors Engineering of Software User Interfaces — Part 2: Accessibility (2008) (incorporated by reference, see 702.4.1) listed below:
L880:   1. Section 9.3.3 Enable sequential entry of multiple (chorded) keystrokes;
L881:   2. Section 9.3.4 Provide adjustment of delay before key acceptance;
L882:   3. Section 9.3.5 Provide adjustment of same-key double-strike acceptance;
L883:   4. Section 10.6.7 Allow users to choose visual alternative for audio output;
L884:   5. Section 10.6.8 Synchronize audio equivalents for visual events;
L885:   6. Section 10.6.9 Provide speech output services; and
L886:   7. Section 10.7.1 Display any captions provided.
L887: ### 503 Applications
L888: 
L889: #### 503.1 General
L890: 
L891: Applications shall conform to 503.
L892: 
L893: #### 503.2 User Preferences
L894: 
L895: Applications shall permit user preferences from platform settings for color, contrast, font type, font size, and focus cursor.
L896: EXCEPTION: Applications that are designed to be isolated from their underlying platform software, including Web applications, shall not be required to conform to 503.2.
L897: #### 503.3 Alternative User Interfaces
L898: 
L899: Where an application provides an alternative user interface that functions as assistive technology, the application shall use platform and other industry standard accessibility services.
L900: 
L901: #### 503.4 User Controls for Captions and Audio Description
L902: 
L903: Where ICT displays video with synchronized audio, ICT shall provide user controls for closed captions and audio descriptions conforming to 503.4.

L428: ##### C205.2.1 Word Substitution when Applying WCAG to Non-Web Software
L429: 
L430: For non-Web software, wherever the term “Web page” or “page” appears in WCAG 2.0 Level A and AA Success Criteria and Conformance Requirements, the term “software” shall be substituted for the terms “Web page” and “page.” In addition, in Success Criterion 1.4.2, the phrase “in software” shall be substituted for the phrase “on a Web page.”
L431: #### C205.3 Complete Processes for Non-Web Software
L432: 
L433: Where non-Web software requires multiple steps to accomplish an activity, all software related to the activity to be accomplished shall conform to WCAG 2.0 as specified in C205.2.
L434: 
L435: ### C206 Support Documentation and Services
L436: #### C206.1 General
L437: 
L438: Where support documentation and services are provided for telecommunications equipment and customer premises equipment, manufacturers shall ensure that such documentation and services conform to Chapter 6 and are made available upon request at no additional charge.
L439: 
L440: * * *
L441: 
L442: # Appendix C to Part 1194 – Functional Performance Criteria and Technical Requirements
L443: 
L444: ## Chapter 3: Functional Performance Criteria
L445: 
L446: ### 301 General
L447: #### 301.1 Scope
L448: 
L449: The requirements of Chapter 3 shall apply to ICT where required by 508 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), 255 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), and where otherwise referenced in any other chapter of the Revised 508 Standards or Revised 255 Guidelines.
L450: 
L451: ### 302 Functional Performance Criteria
L452: 
L453: #### 302.1 Without Vision
L454: 
L455: Where a visual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that does not require user vision.
L456: #### 302.2 With Limited Vision
L457: 
L458: Where a visual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that enables users to make use of limited vision.
L459: 
L460: #### 302.3 Without Perception of Color
L461: 
L462: Where a visual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one visual mode of operation that does not require user perception of color.
L463: #### 302.4 Without Hearing
L464: 
L465: Where an audible mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that does not require user hearing.
L466: 
L467: #### 302.5 With Limited Hearing
L468: 
L469: Where an audible mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that enables users to make use of limited hearing.
L470: 
L471: #### 302.6 Without Speech
L472: 
L473: Where speech is used for input, control, or operation, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that does not require user speech.
L474: #### 302.7 With Limited Manipulation
L475: 
L476: Where a manual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that does not require fine motor control or simultaneous manual operations.
L477: 
L478: #### 302.8 With Limited Reach and Strength
L479: 
L480: Where a manual mode of operation is provided, ICT shall provide at least one mode of operation that is operable with limited reach and limited strength.
L481: #### 302.9 With Limited Language, Cognitive, and Learning Abilities
L482: 
L483: ICT shall provide features making its use by individuals with limited cognitive, language, and learning abilities simpler and easier.
L484: 
L485: * * *
L486: 
L487: ## Chapter 4: Hardware
L488: 
L489: ### 401 General
L490: #### 401.1 Scope
L491: 
L492: The requirements of Chapter 4 shall apply to ICT that is hardware where required by 508 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), 255 Chapter 2 (Scoping Requirements), and where otherwise referenced in any other chapter of the Revised 508 Standards or Revised 255 Guidelines.
L493: EXCEPTION: Hardware that is assistive technology shall not be required to conform to the requirements of this chapter.
L494: 
L495: ### 402 Closed Functionality
L496: #### 402.1 General
L497: 
L498: ICT with closed functionality shall be operable without requiring the user to attach or install assistive technology other than personal headsets or other audio couplers, and shall conform to 402.
L499: #### 402.2 Speech-Output Enabled
L500: 
L501: ICT with a display screen shall be speech-output enabled for full and independent use by individuals with vision impairments.
L502: EXCEPTIONS:
L503:   1. Variable message signs conforming to 402.5 shall not be required to be speech-output enabled.
L504:   2. Speech output shall not be required where ICT display screens only provide status indicators and those indicators conform to 409.
L505:   3. Where speech output cannot be supported due to constraints in available memory or processor capability, ICT shall be permitted to conform to 409 in lieu of 402.2.
L506:   4. Audible tones shall be permitted instead of speech output where the content of user input is not displayed as entered for security purposes, including, but not limited to, asterisks representing personal identification numbers.
L507:   5. Speech output shall not be required for: the machine location; date and time of transaction; customer account number; and the machine identifier or label.
L508:   6. Speech output shall not be required for advertisements and other similar information unless they convey information that can be used for the transaction being conducted.
L509: ##### 402.2.1 Information Displayed On-Screen
L510: 
L511: Speech output shall be provided for all information displayed on-screen.
L512: 
L513: ##### 402.2.2 Transactional Outputs
L514: 
L515: Where transactional outputs are provided, the speech output shall audibly provide all information necessary to verify a transaction.
L516: ##### 402.2.3 Speech Delivery Type and Coordination
L517: 
L518: Speech output shall be delivered through a mechanism that is readily available to all users, including, but not limited to, an industry standard connector or a telephone handset. Speech shall be recorded or digitized human, or synthesized. Speech output shall be coordinated with information displayed on the screen.
L519: ##### 402.2.4 User Control
L520: 
L521: Speech output for any single function shall be automatically interrupted when a transaction is selected. Speech output shall be capable of being repeated and paused.
L522: ##### 402.2.5 Braille Instructions
L523: 
L524: Where speech output is required by 402.2, braille instructions for initiating the speech mode of operation shall be provided. Braille shall be contracted and shall conform to 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix D, Section 703.3.1.
L525: EXCEPTION: Devices for personal use shall not be required to conform to 402.2.5.
L526: #### 402.3 Volume
L527: 
L528: ICT that delivers sound, including speech output required by 402.2, shall provide volume control and output amplification conforming to 402.3.
L529: EXCEPTION: ICT conforming to 412.2 shall not be required to conform to 402.3.
L530: ##### 402.3.1 Private Listening
L531: 
L532: Where ICT provides private listening, it shall provide a mode of operation for controlling the volume. Where ICT delivers output by an audio transducer typically held up to the ear, a means for effective magnetic wireless coupling to hearing technologies shall be provided.
L533: ##### 402.3.2 Non-private Listening
L534: 
L535: Where ICT provides non-private listening, incremental volume control shall be provided with output amplification up to a level of at least 65 dB. A function shall be provided to automatically reset the volume to the default level after every use.

L61: # Structural Navigation
L62: 
L63: Orca's Structural Navigation feature allows you to navigate amongst elements in a document. The types of elements by which you can navigate include:
L64: 
L65:   * Headings and other text blocks
L66: 
L67:   * Form controls
L68: 
L69:   * Links
L70: 
L71:   * Lists and list items
L72: 
L73:   * Landmarks, separators, and anchors
L74: 
L75:   * Tables and table cells
L76: 
L77: A full list of individual elements and their associated keybindings can be found in 【49†Structural Navigation Commands】.
L78: ## Supported Applications
L79: Currently, Structural Navigation is fully implemented for web content, including the help content you are reading now. Orca's Structural Navigation support for table cells has also been implemented for OpenOffice Writer and LibreOffice Writer. Implementing the remainder of the Structural Navigation objects to these office suites requires changes to be made by their respective developers.
L80: Implementing any Structural Navigation features within Evince will require a similar effort on the part of its developers.
L81: ### Don't Forget To Toggle Structural Navigation On!
L82: 
L83: Depending on where you are, it may be necessary for you to explicitly toggle Structural Navigation on before you can use it.
L84: ### When Toggling Structural Navigation On Is Required
L85: 
L86: In web pages, explicitly toggling Structural Navigation on is generally unnecessary because your interaction with the document largely consists of reading its content. Thus there is no question as to whether the 'H' you just pressed was meant to be a writing command or a navigation command.
L87: On the other hand, in editable documents such as those found in OpenOffice and LibreOffice, it is far more difficult for Orca to accurately predict what you expect to have happen as a result of pressing 'H'. Therefore, before you can use any Structural Navigation command in an editable document, you must first toggle Structural Navigation on by pressing `Orca Modifier`+`Z`. When you are finished navigating and ready to resume writing, press `Orca Modifier`+`Z` again to toggle Structural Navigation off.
L88: ## Available Settings
L89: 
L90: In addition to the aforementioned commands, Orca has a number of configurable options available specifically for applications in which there is structural navigation support.
L91: ### Configuring Structural Navigation
L92: 
L93:   1. Give focus to an application for which Orca has Structural Navigation support.
L94: 
L95:   2. Get into the 【46†Orca Preferences】 dialog box for the current application by pressing `Ctrl`+`Orca Modifier`+`Space`.
L96: 
L97:   3. Navigate to the last page of the dialog box which should be named according to the name of your current application.
L98: 
L99:   4. Examine and change the settings as you see fit.
L100: 
L101:   5. Press the OK button.

L63: # Flat Review Commands
